evaluator: E12 – Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), re-check of E11's conditions, persona: image-analysis specialist in a bioimaging core facility who writes Fiji macros and Python daily, cares about reproducibility, provenance and ImageJ-identical results, and has used napari, QuPath and Icy
method: Short re-check of E11's three conditions (E10-3, E11-2, E11-1), the provenance leftover E10-4 and the new script-editor syntax highlighting, using E11's controls and sequences, plus a short regression pass. Nobody told me how anything was fixed. I read E11's evaluation.json only, not docs/USABILITY.md, other evaluators' files or the source. Tooling: Playwright from the e2e venv, headless Google Chrome (channel=chrome), 1440×900, run as 18 short sequential scripts with one browser at a time. Each script reused my client id baa1624268004189 through sessionStorage, so my server session and recorder stayed continuous. Evidence: DOM/ARIA facts and computed styles, /api/state, /api/recorder/preview, /api/recorder/ijm (all with my X-Lumen-Client header), Results rows, screenshots in shots/, and TIFF Info dumps (tifffile from the project .venv, run with -I). Reference values came from PIL on the cached sample GIFs. memory_pressure: 50 % free at the start, 48 % at the end. Start state: 0 images, 0 ROIs, 0 Results rows, so no Close All was needed. Regression pass: Gaussian Sigma 'abc' + Enter; Unsharp Mask with an invalid Weight '0..6' and Enter pressed in the valid Radius field; the IJM export of the Blobs (25K) open; ImageJ's Gel sample (another GIF) checked for type, LUT and a whole-image Measure against PIL; Close All's unsaved-changes dialog. Not covered: a real folder batch run, screen reader, several users. Clean-up: File ▸ Close All (5 images, 'Close without saving'); Results cleared through 'Clear…' → 'Delete 2 rows'; my recorder cleared (count 0); no ROIs or tables were created. My three Open Recent entries (gel.gif, saved_max_e12.tif, blobs.gif) were removed from lumen.session.recent, and the three older entries the cap of 20 had pushed out were re-appended, so the list equals its pre-test content. ~/.lumen/recent.json was restored byte-identical from the backup in eval_e12/. Side effect: Open Sample ▸ Gel downloaded gel.gif into ~/.lumen/samples (a sample cache, left in place). Final /api/state: 0 images, 0 ROIs, 0 Results rows, 0 tables. No Chrome/Playwright process is left.

reassessment.evidence: Blobs (25K) → Process ▸ Filters ▸ Median…, a click into the Radius field (input#p-radius, role=spinbutton), then the value. 'abc': aria-invalid=true, inline message 'Radius is not a number', Apply disabled with title 'Radius: type a number first'. With focus still in the field, Enter leaves the sheet open, the value 'abc' and the message stay, focus stays in the field, and nothing is recorded (recorder count 3 before and after, last line still the Gaussian, image rev unchanged at 1, no new log entry). '2,5,1' + Enter: identical (aria-invalid=true, same message, sheet stays open, count 3, rev 1). A valid '3' + Enter: aria-invalid cleared, Apply enabled, Enter closes the sheet, the recorder gains lumen.run("filters.median", radius=3.0, shape='disk', scope='slice'), log 'Median (20 ms)', rev 1 → 2. No toast in any case; the inline red message is the only feedback. Screenshots shots/30_median_abc_before.png, shots/30_median_abc_after.png, shots/31_median_2_5_1_before.png, shots/31_median_2_5_1_after.png, shots/32_median_3_before.png.
reassessment.comment: Enter is now blocked the same way the Apply click is: an invalid entry never silently becomes the default radius, and a valid entry still confirms with Enter as in Fiji. A tiny extra cue on the blocked Enter (a shake or a focus on the message) would be nice, but the persistent red message next to the field is enough.

reassessment.comment: Provenance now reads correctly. An image born in memory says what it was derived from, with parameters, and doesn't claim to come from itself. A re-opened file keeps the earlier history and adds the true Source. Cosmetic leftovers: every line now carries a 'Lumen processing:' prefix, which is verbose to read in ImageJ's Show Info but harmless. As E11 noted, the derived-from line says axis='Z' (correct here, since I projected slices).

reassessment.evidence: Docked editor (Script & Recorder section): textarea and the .code-hl layer (PRE.code-hl inside .code-layer) have identical metrics (JetBrains Mono 12px / line-height 17.4px / padding 4px 8px, white-space pre, tab-size 4). The textarea text is transparent (color and -webkit-text-fill-color rgba(0,0,0,0)), so there is no ghost text, and the caret is light (rgb 232,234,240). Python spans: hl-com comment, hl-kw import/as/def/return/if/else/None/True/print, hl-bi numpy/np/float/lumen, hl-fn stats/mean, hl-str including a triple-quoted docstring and single quotes, hl-num 3/1.0/0/0x1F, hl-op. A 270-character line scrolls horizontally with the colours in step (textarea scrollLeft 1719 = code-hl scrollLeft 1719, scrollWidth 2002 both, also after a horizontal wheel), screenshots shots/55_docked_long_line_end.png, shots/57_docked_long_line_wheel.png. Esc in the docked editor moves focus to the image (DIV.canvas-wrap). Large view (palette 'Script Editor in a Large View', .script-editor.large): the textarea is 13px / 18.85px, but the colour layer stays at 12px / 17.4px. So the invisible text that owns the caret and selection is larger than the coloured text people see. Measured: (a) on a 20-line script, clicking on the visible 'v08', 'v15' and 'v20' puts the caret into lines 7, 14 and 19; typing 'ZZ' after clicking the visible 'v15' turns line 14 into 'ZZv14 = 14  # line 14' (shots/64_large_click_v15_typed.png, where the gutter numbers also drift: '14' sits beside 'v15'); (b) a 3-character selection at value[48:51]='fgh' is drawn over 'ija'/'jab' about three characters to the right (shots/62_large_col40_sel3.png), and the Shift-selection of 'lumen.image' on line 6 is drawn half a line low (shots/53b_editor_selection_zoom.png); (c) at the end of the long line the textarea has scrollLeft 1123 / scrollWidth 2168 but the colour layer has 957 / 2002, so the caret sits 166 px from the visible text. ImageJ macro colours (large view, language 'ImageJ macro'): hl-com, hl-kw for/if/macro, hl-bi getTitle/run/nSlices/getPixel/print, hl-str, hl-num, hl-op; but setSlice is coloured hl-fn (user function) instead of built-in (shots/60_large_ijm.png). ⌘R in the large view ran the script: output 'NAME opened_then_saved_e12.tif 23.78387451171875 single 31 True None', no page reload (shots/54_editor_cmd_r.png). Esc in the large view closes it and returns focus to the image (DIV.canvas-wrap).
reassessment.comment: The highlighting itself is good and readable, and in the docked editor everything I checked works: typing, caret, selection, Esc, ⌘R and horizontal scrolling. The large view, which is where I'd actually write a script, has a font-size mismatch between the input layer and the colour layer. From about line 7 on, a click lands on the line above the one I see, selections are drawn off the text, and the caret drifts by several characters on long lines. That makes it easy to edit the wrong line of an analysis script without noticing. Logged as regression E12-1. The setSlice colouring is cosmetic.

regressions.heuristic: Consistency / Error prevention (what you see is what you edit)
regressions.location: Script editor, large view (palette 'Script Editor in a Large View' or the expand button in Script & Recorder), all languages
regressions.observation: The new syntax-colour layer and the editable textarea have different metrics in the large view: textarea 13px / line-height 18.85px, colour layer 12px / 17.4px. (In the docked editor both are 12px / 17.4px.) The textarea text is transparent, so what you see is the colour layer, while the caret, selection, clicks and line-number gutter follow the textarea. From line ~7 on, a click on a visible line puts the caret into the line above. Typing after clicking the visible 'v15' changed line 14. Selections are drawn up to half a line low and several characters to the right, and on a 270-character line the caret is 166 px away from the visible text it edits.
regressions.evidence: shots/64_large_click_v15_typed.png (clicks on visible v08/v15/v20 → caret lines 7/14/19, 'ZZv14' after clicking v15), shots/62_large_col40_sel3.png, shots/53b_editor_selection_zoom.png, shots/61_large_long_end.png; computed styles textarea 13px/18.85px vs .code-hl 12px/17.4px; scrollLeft 1123 vs 957, scrollWidth 2168 vs 2002.

regressions.location: Image tabs after a page reload
regressions.observation: After ⌘S the tab correctly switches from the modified dot to a plain × (screenshot 43_after_cmd_s.png). After reloading the page, the same saved images show the dot again, with the tab tooltip '● modified (1 undoable step)' and the close button labelled 'Close saved_max_e12.tif (unsaved changes)'. 'Modified' is apparently rebuilt from the undo history and forgets the save. It errs on the safe side, so the only cost is a false 'unsaved' warning. I can't tell whether this predates the current fixes.
regressions.evidence: shots/43_after_cmd_s.png vs shots/50_script_section.png / shots/58_after_esc_docked.png; DOM: tab class 'tab modified', title '… ● modified (1 undoable step) …', aria-label 'Close saved_max_e12.tif (unsaved changes)'. At clean-up, File ▸ Close All said '3 of them have unsaved changes (“blobs.gif”, “saved_max_e12.tif”, “opened_then_saved_e12.tif”; the undo history)'. Both .tif files had been saved with ⌘S after their last change (shots/80_close_all_dialog.png).

regressions.observation: The macro built-ins getTitle, run, nSlices, getPixel and print are coloured as built-ins (hl-bi), but setSlice, also an ImageJ built-in, is coloured as a user function (hl-fn), the same as a user's own function call. This is cosmetic.

positives: Enter is now blocked for non-numeric input in every sheet I tried (Median 'abc' and '2,5,1', Gaussian 'abc', Unsharp Mask with an invalid second field while Enter is pressed in the first), and a valid value still confirms with Enter. The inline message names the field ('Weight is not a number').

ImageJ's Blobs (25K) is now 8-bit with an inverting LUT, and its whole-image Measure is identical to ImageJ (Mean 103.269, Min 8, Max 248). The cursor readout gives raw values. Gel.gif also matches its raw values (Mean 150.441, Min 9, Max 200).
The folder-batch default list drops the ImageJ-sample open like any other open, and the IJM export writes the correct run("Blobs (25K)").
TIFF provenance is now right: no self-referencing Source for an in-memory image, derived-from with parameters, and a true Source plus a preserved history for a re-opened file.

Syntax colouring for Python and ImageJ macro is clear, with distinct comment, keyword, built-in, function, string, number and operator colours. In the docked editor it stays exactly aligned, also when scrolling a long line horizontally. Esc returns to the image, and ⌘R runs the script without reloading the page.
Close All lists which images have unsaved changes and offers Cancel. Results Clear… names the row count and offers 'Undo clear'.
overall: All three of E11's conditions are met on this build, and so is the provenance leftover. Enter no longer turns 'abc' into the default radius, the folder batch no longer re-opens Blobs on every file, Blobs (25K) measures exactly as in ImageJ, and a projected image no longer names itself as its own Source. So yes, I would now hand Lumen to Fiji users on a single-user facility workstation, with one warning. Use the docked script editor, not the large view, until E12-1 is fixed. In the large view the new colour layer is drawn at a smaller font than the text you actually edit, so from line ~7 on a click edits the line above the one you see, which is unacceptable for analysis scripts. It is a one-line CSS mismatch and the docked editor is fine, so I treat it as a must-fix but not a hand-over blocker. A false 'unsaved' marker after a page reload is minor. My earlier caveats about a shared multi-user server still apply (not re-tested).
